record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Closed 3-manifolds of Heegaard genus two can be represented by 4-colored graphs constructed from six positive integers arranged as (n_1, h_1; n_2, h_2; n_3, h_3). Determine the relations between two such 6-tuples that make their colored graphs represent the same 3-manifold, and classify the homeomorphism types of Heegaard genus two 3-manifolds in terms of these representing 6-tuples.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A 4-colored graph is a finite multigraph $\Gamma=(V(\Gamma),E(\Gamma))$ together with an edge-coloring $\gamma:E(\Gamma)\to\{0,1,2,3\}$ such that any two edges meeting at a common vertex have distinct colors (in particular, $\Gamma$ is 4-regular). Such a graph determines a 3-dimensional pseudocomplex $K(\Gamma)$ by associating to each vertex a tetrahedron, identifying $i$-faces of two tetrahedra whenever the corresponding vertices are joined by an edge of color $i$, and the topological space $|K(\Gamma)|$ is called the geometric realization. A 4-colored graph $\Gamma$ is said to represent a closed 3-manifold $M^3$ if $|K(\Gamma)|\cong M^3$.

It is known that every closed orientable 3-manifold of Heegaard genus at most two can be represented by a 4-colored graph constructed from a 6-tuple of positive integers
$$(n_1,h_1;\,n_2,h_2;\,n_3,h_3),$$
according to the following standard construction: for each $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ one builds an elementary "block" depending on the parameters $(n_i,h_i)$, and the three blocks are assembled using the colors $\{0,1,2,3\}$ to obtain a 4-colored graph $\Gamma(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ whose associated pseudocomplex is a closed 3-manifold of Heegaard genus $\le 2$.

Problem. 
(a) Determine an explicit set of moves/relations on 6-tuples $(n_1,h_1;n_2,h_2;n_3,h_3)$ of positive integers such that two such 6-tuples give rise to 4-colored graphs representing the same closed 3-manifold (up to homeomorphism) if and only if they are related by a finite sequence of these moves.

(b) Using (a), give a complete classification of the homeomorphism types of closed orientable 3-manifolds of Heegaard genus at most two in terms of equivalence classes of 6-tuples under these relations.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: a G-equivalence relation on 6-tuples is known to preserve the represented genus-two 3-manifold, and catalogues of prime genus-two 3-manifolds of small complexity (e.g. 78 prime 3-manifolds of complexity ≤ 21) have been compiled. However, a complete set of moves giving a sufficient and necessary equivalence, together with a full homeomorphism classification in terms of 6-tuples, does not appear to have been established. The problem appears to remain open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Three-manifolds with Heegaard genus at most two represented by crystallisations with at most 42 vertices
status_evidence.snippet: A catalogue of prime 3-manifolds of genus two of complexity ≤ 21 represented by crystallisations determined by 6-tuples.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification via tabulation up to bounded complexity; full classification not established.

status_evidence.title: Graphs encoding 3-manifolds of genus 2
status_evidence.snippet: A G-equivalence on 6-tuples is introduced that preserves the associated genus-two 3-manifold.
status_evidence.claim: Known relations preserve the manifold but completeness is not proven.

status_evidence.title: Compact 3-manifolds via 4-colored graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of 4-colored graph representations of compact 3-manifolds, including the genus-two case.
status_evidence.claim: Reference framework for the 6-tuple representation problem.
